mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-01.title: Apply the rule
mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-01.body:
$7 - 6 + 9 - a + 2 = 12 - a$. For a digit $a$, $12 - a$ is between 3 and 12, and the only multiple of 11 there is 11, so $a = 1$. Check: $76{,}912 = 11 \times 6992$ ✓.

**Answer: 1**

mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-01.title: Divide directly
mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-01.body:
$76{,}902 = 11 \times 6991 + 1$, so $76{,}902$ leaves remainder 1. Adding $10a$ must fix this: $10a \equiv -1 \equiv 10 \pmod{11}$, so $a = 1$.

**Answer: 1**

mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-02.title: Count outcomes
mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-02.body:
Of the $6 \times 6 = 36$ equally likely outcomes, a sum of 11 comes from (5, 6) and (6, 5): $\frac{2}{36} = \frac{1}{18}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1}{18}$**

mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-02.title: First die then second
mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-02.body:
The first die must be 5 or 6 ($\frac26$), and then the second die must be the one number that makes 11 ($\frac16$): $\frac26 \cdot \frac16 = \frac1{18}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1}{18}$**

mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-03.title: Even, and digit sum divisible by 3
mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-03.body:
A four-digit palindrome is $abba$. To be even, its last digit $a$ is even; the largest choice is $a = 8$. Its digit sum $2a + 2b = 16 + 2b$ must be divisible by 3, so $2b \equiv 2 \pmod 3$, i.e. $b \in \{1, 4, 7\}$. The largest is $b = 7$: **8778** ($= 6 \times 1463$).

**Answer: 8778**

mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-03.title: Check from the top
mathcounts-potw-2026-11-02-03.body:
Palindromes starting with 9 end in 9 (odd), so try 8998, 8888, 8778, …: digit sums 34, 32, 30. Only 8778 has digit sum divisible by 3, so it is the first multiple of 6.

**Answer: 8778**
